correctness.publicDocumentationImpact: Existing sessions-and-review.md already describes static rotating status indicators under reduced motion. No new setting, label, or user procedure. The implementation-specific design paragraph is updated.

The shared component change also affects transient Spinner uses; default motion is unchanged.

conclusions.normalMode: Mixed CPU results. No broad normal-mode speed claim is attributed to this reduced-motion rule. Normal-idle first pair main CPU rises 40.17% and renderer CPU rises 34.84%.
conclusions.frames: Frame-gap p95 is neutral by median paired change in all modes. Reduced-motion maximum gaps worsen in four pairs; final candidate gap rises from 33.4 to 333.32 ms. Normal-idle pair 2 maximum rises 16.8 to 66.7 ms. Streaming pair 1 p95 rises 16.8 to 33.3 ms.
conclusions.animationCountOutlier: Normal idle retains 51 running animations in every sample. Candidate streaming pair 4 records 42, while other streaming samples record 51; its owner is not established. Panel/editor and ordered-update witnesses still pass. Do not infer normal-mode benefit from fewer animations.
conclusions.traffic: Both versions have zero resets, zero HTTP failures, and zero plugin conversation reads across measured windows. Scheduled core backfill remains, usually 24 or 25 reads per window.
conclusions.cpuDomains: ThreadTime is main-renderer-thread CPU. ProcessTime is renderer-process CPU and includes the main thread. Do not add them. TaskDuration, style, and layout durations are elapsed task work, not CPU measurements.

limits: Linux Chromium measurements do not prove M2 Air performance, battery savings, field INP, or a memory leak.
Existing original-baseline comparisons retain their own build identities; do not multiply their gains by this isolated comparison.
Normal CPU and frame-gap regressions remain unattributed. Their samples are retained.
Native application hide/restore tests are separate and not counted among the passing checks here.
